transcript: One of the most fundamental debates in international relations is how to maintain peace between competing nation-states. Do governments seek to maximize security or power? Americans must wrestle with these questions because they're bigger than faculty lounge banter. They are the starting point of foreign policy in the foundation of national security. More often than not, you can trace the political disagreements about America's foreign policy that you read in the news back to these basic questions. Whether it's China, Russia, Iran, or the pullout from Afghanistan, the Biden administration is wrestling day in and day out with these calculations. The deterrent side of this debate was perhaps most eloquently articulated by former President Ronald Reagan when he talked about peace through strength and how securing an overwhelming strategic advantage for America makes the world more stable, not less. And for today's episode of the podcast, I have the privilege of interviewing one of America's foremost defenders of the piece through strength approach today, United States Senator Ted Cruz.
